usdRate.sourceName: World Bank WDI, official exchange rate (PA.NUS.FCRF), Qatar
usdRate.note: The riyal is pegged at 3.64 per US dollar. CLDR gives no narrow symbol (only 'QAR'); the Arabic abbreviation ر.ق is used locally.

inflation_cpi.sourceName: Trading Economics, citing the National Planning Council (NPC), CPI August 2026
inflation_cpi.note: Consumer prices up 4.09% year on year in August 2026 (3.98% in July), the highest reading since March; secondary source because the NPC site could not be read (certificate error). World Bank 2024 average 1.3%.

inflation_projection.sourceName: Dollar peg; 2005-2026 average CPI inflation of about 2.1% (Trading Economics, citing NPC)
inflation_projection.note: With the riyal pegged to the dollar, inflation has averaged about 2% over two decades, so 2% a year is used for long-range plans.

policy_rate.sourceName: Trading Economics, Qatar Central Bank decision of 16 September 2026
policy_rate.note: The QCB raised its deposit rate (QCBDR) by 25 bps to 4.10%, with the lending rate at 4.60% and the repo rate at 4.35%; secondary source because the QCB site could not be read (certificate error). The deposit rate is used as the policy rate.

savings_account_rate.note: Average savings-account rates are published in QCB statistics, but the QCB site could not be read (certificate error) and no other official source was found.

fdr_3m_rate.note: Average 3-month time-deposit rates are in QCB statistics, which could not be read (certificate error).

fdr_1y_rate.note: Average 1-year time-deposit rates are in QCB statistics, which could not be read (certificate error).

dps_rate.note: No industry-wide rate for a monthly recurring deposit product was found.

bank_deposit_avg_rate.sourceName: World Bank WDI, deposit interest rate (FR.INR.DPST), Qatar
bank_deposit_avg_rate.note: 4.68% in 2025 (IMF International Financial Statistics via the World Bank); the fresher QCB statistics could not be read.

sanchayapatra_5y_rate.note: No government savings certificate or retail savings bond for individuals was found; QCB treasury bills and government bonds are auctioned to banks.

tbill_91d_rate.note: The QCB auctions 3-, 6- and 9-month treasury bills to banks each month, but the auction results on the QCB site could not be read (certificate error).

tbond_5y_rate.note: No current 5-year government bond yield was found from an official or allowed secondary source.

tbond_10y_rate.note: The only 10-year yield found (Trading Economics) dates from February 2023, too old to use; the QCB site could not be read.

tax_bank_interest.sourceName: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries, Qatar, individual income determination
tax_bank_interest.note: Bank interest and returns due to individuals not carrying on a taxable activity are not subject to income tax, and salaries are untaxed.

tax_sanchayapatra_profit.sourceName: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries, Qatar, individual income determination
tax_sanchayapatra_profit.note: Capital gains on securities are exempt for individuals and there is no tax on bank interest or returns; no retail savings certificate exists.

deposit_insurance_limit.note: No deposit insurance scheme or cover limit could be confirmed; the QCB site could not be read (certificate error).

credit_card_rate_cap.note: No legal cap or published average credit card rate could be read; the QCB site could not be read (certificate error).

equity_return_low.sourceName: QCB deposit rate 4.10% (September 2026); weak 10-year record of Qatar's main index
equity_return_low.note: Low case: the local index, which ended the last decade close to where it started, returns less than deposits.

equity_return_base.sourceName: QCB deposit rate 4.10%; World Bank deposit rate 4.68% (2025)
equity_return_base.note: Base case: about 2.5 points above the safe deposit rate, below the 4-point cap, because the main Qatari index has had a weak, dividend-driven 10-year record.

equity_return_high.sourceName: QCB deposit rate 4.10%; Gulf equity premium
equity_return_high.note: High case: a fuller equity premium if Gulf markets re-rate.

gold_return_low.sourceName: Dollar peg (3.64 QAR per USD); World Bank exchange rate
gold_return_low.note: Low case: flat dollar gold; the peg means no currency boost.

gold_return_base.sourceName: Dollar peg (3.64 QAR per USD); long-run dollar gold trend
gold_return_base.note: Base case: the long-run dollar gold trend of about 4% a year, with no depreciation gain under the peg.

gold_return_high.sourceName: Dollar peg (3.64 QAR per USD); long-run dollar gold trend
gold_return_high.note: High case: strong dollar gold years.

fixed_income_return_low.sourceName: QCB deposit rate 4.10% (September 2026); World Bank deposit rate 4.68% (2025)
fixed_income_return_low.note: Low case: deposit rates fall with US rates, untaxed.

fixed_income_return_base.sourceName: QCB deposit rate 4.10% (September 2026); World Bank deposit rate 4.68% (2025)
fixed_income_return_base.note: Base case: a little below today's untaxed deposit rates, allowing for rate cuts over a long plan.

fixed_income_return_high.sourceName: World Bank deposit rate 4.68% (2025); QCB lending rate 4.60%
fixed_income_return_high.note: High case: deposit rates stay near their 2025 level.

life_claim_settlement_rate.note: The QCB (the insurance regulator) publishes no industry-wide life claim settlement ratio that could be found.

insurance_term_premium_table.note: Term life cover is sold, but no published premium rates per QAR 1,000 of cover by age were found from the regulator or another public source.

health_hospitalisation_cost.note: No published typical cost of a major private hospital stay was found.

health_premium_table.note: No published private health insurance premiums by age were found from a public source.

oop_health_share.sourceName: World Bank WDI, out-of-pocket expenditure (% of current health expenditure), Qatar
oop_health_share.note: 7.4% in 2023 (WHO Global Health Expenditure Database via the World Bank); older than 2025, the latest available.

goal_inflation_health.sourceName: Inflation assumption 2%; health CPI about 0% (May 2026, Trading Economics citing NPC)
goal_inflation_health.note: Public care keeps the health CPI near zero, but private treatment costs usually rise faster than prices, so 1.5 points above the inflation assumption.

goal_inflation_education.sourceName: Inflation assumption 2%; education CPI 2.1% (January 2026, Trading Economics citing NPC)
goal_inflation_education.note: Education prices rose about 2% a year recently; private school fees tend to rise faster, so 1.5 points above the inflation assumption.

life_expectancy.sourceName: World Bank WDI, life expectancy at birth, total (SP.DYN.LE00.IN), Qatar
life_expectancy.note: 82.5 years in 2024 (men 81.8, women 83.5); the population is mostly younger migrant workers.

life_table_remaining.sourceName: UN World Population Prospects 2024 via populationpyramid.net
life_table_remaining.note: Secondary source of UN WPP 2024 medium variant for 2026; totals at 60, 70 and 80 are the mean of men and women (only the 65 total is published there).

support_ratio.sourceName: World Bank SP.POP.DPND.OL (2025); UN WPP 2024 via populationpyramid.net (2040, 2065)
support_ratio.note: 100 / old-age dependency ratio: 2.04 (2025, World Bank), 2.4 (2040) and 4.5 (2065, populationpyramid.net/qatar/2065/); the very large migrant workforce keeps the ratio high.

retirement_age_default.note: Social Insurance Law No. 1 of 2022 (General Retirement and Social Insurance Authority) covers Qatari private-sector workers, but the pension age could not be read from the authority's pages (content not loaded) or the law text.

retirement_age_government.note: The civil retirement rules under Law No. 1 of 2022 could not be read from the General Retirement and Social Insurance Authority site.

retirement_return_low.note: Low case: deposit rates fall with US rates, untaxed.

retirement_return_base.sourceName: QCB deposit rate 4.10%; World Bank deposit rate 4.68% (2025)
retirement_return_base.note: Base case: below today's untaxed deposit rates (no 1-year rate could be read), so it does not exceed the safe rate.

retirement_return_high.note: High case: deposit rates stay near their 2025 level.

retirement_accumulation_return_low.sourceName: QCB deposit rate 4.10%; equity low case 3%
retirement_accumulation_return_low.note: Low case: a mix earning about deposit rates.

retirement_accumulation_return_base.sourceName: QCB deposit rate 4.10%; equity base 6.5%; gold base 4%
retirement_accumulation_return_base.note: Base case: a balanced mix of deposits or sukuk, equities and some gold.

old_age_allowance_monthly.note: Social security assistance for older Qatari nationals exists through the Ministry of Social Development and Family, but no current monthly amount could be read from an official source.

old_age_allowance_eligibility.note: Eligibility rules for social security assistance to older people could not be read from an official source.

gratuity_rule.note: The Labour Law (No. 14 of 2004) provides an end-of-service gratuity for workers, but the article giving the weeks of wages per year could not be opened on the Al Meezan legal portal or ILO NATLEX (access refused).

public_pension_scheme.note: The General Retirement and Social Insurance Authority says Social Insurance Law No. 1 of 2022 (issued 19 April 2022) covers Qatari government and private-sector employees and self-employed Qataris, but the pension age and indexation rules could not be read; expatriates are not covered.

dps.note: No standard monthly recurring deposit product was found.

sanchayapatra_5y.note: No government savings certificate for individuals was found.

tbill_91d.note: Issued monthly by the QCB for 3, 6 and 9 months and bought by banks; individuals reach them only through banks or funds.

tbond_5y.note: Government bonds and sukuk are auctioned to banks.

tbond_10y.note: Government bonds and sukuk are auctioned to banks.

equity_fund.note: Funds investing in Qatari and Gulf shares are offered to retail investors.

gold.note: Gold bars, coins and jewellery are freely sold.

insuranceComplaints.name: Qatar Central Bank, consumer protection
insuranceComplaints.note: Complaints about insurers go to the QCB consumer protection function.

pensionScheme.name: General Retirement and Social Insurance Authority

publicHealthCover.name: Ministry of Public Health (public health care)
